_comment: Host-parity ratchet floor (scripts/check_host_parity.py). These two numbers may only go DOWN. unreachable is 0 because kernel_op exposes appearance and the sites customer stack; 3 routes are WALLED on purpose (billing x2 platform-domain, sites/db/reveal credential bytes) and walled is tracked separately, never ratcheted. unreviewed counts the routes still awaiting classification. An area leaves it when a host tool covers it (`editor` covers /api/vscode; `autofill` covers the browser-forms routes by op, while capture, save and grant-creation stay the USER's act by design, named in _AREA_HOST_TOOLS; `embedding_route` covers /api/media-embedding through its media_* ops rather than a second tool name; `artifact` covers the host's half of the Designs shelf, while browsing, trying and removing designs stay the person's clicks) or when it derives WALLED (the Code Approvals routes under /api/workbench are the person's review surface, no host tool reads them, and read:review / write:review have no entity bits; ask-for-changes is also walled by path in kernel_ops._WALLED_PATHS, which is a decision). /api/security stays unreviewed because classifying it is a decision of its own: all four of its scopes (execute:scan, read:incidents, read:processes, read:network) carry entity bits, so a [] row would read its routes as unreachable against the floor of 0, and covering them means exposing /api/security to kernel_op. Measure with generate_capabilities inside the image the change ships in. Lower a number here in the same change that genuinely improves it.
